item.research_question: How does increasing chemical disorder and compositional complexity in single-phase concentrated solid solution alloys (SP-CSAs) affect energy dissipation pathways and subsequent defect evolution under ion irradiation?
item.material_system: Single-phase fcc concentrated solid solution alloys: elemental Nickel (Ni), binary NiCo, binary NiFe, and quaternary NiCoFeCr (all equiatomic), plus non-equiatomic Ni0.65Fe0.35 and Ni0.40Fe0.60.
item.processing_route: High-purity elemental metals arc melted and drop cast into copper moulds; single crystals directionally solidified in an optical floating zone furnace under Ar atmosphere; polished to damage-free surfaces for ion channelling.
item.test_conditions: Room temperature irradiation using 3 MeV Au2+ ions (fluence 1-2 × 10^13 cm^-2) and 1.5 MeV Ni+ ions (fluence 6 × 10^13 to 2 × 10^14 cm^-2); electrical resistivity measured between 5 K and 300 K; thermal conductivity measured at room temperature; in situ ion channelling and high-resolution TEM characterization.
key_findings: Electrical resistivity at 5 K increases from ~0.1 μΩ cm for Ni to 77.1 μΩ cm for NiCoFeCr, indicating a substantial reduction in electron mean free path.
Total thermal conductivity at 300 K decreases from 88 W m−1 K−1 for Ni to 12.8 W m−1 K−1 for NiCoFeCr.
Backscattering yield (damage indicator) for NiFe is approximately half that of pure Ni after 3 MeV Au irradiation.
Stable defect production in NiFe is ~2 times lower than in pure Ni according to molecular dynamics cascade simulations.
Quaternary NiCoFeCr shows ~5 times less accumulated damage than pure Ni under Ni ion irradiation.
Increasing Fe concentration from 35% to 60% in Ni-Fe alloys enhances irradiation resistance.
Stacking fault tetrahedra (SFT) sizes are smaller in alloys (4.3-4.4 nm) compared to pure Ni (7.0 nm) due to slower defect migration.
item.mechanism: Chemical disorder in SP-CSAs causes significant smearing of the electronic band structure (Bloch spectral function), reducing the electron mean free path and drastically lowering electronic thermal conductivity. This leads to less efficient heat dissipation, prolonging the lifetime of thermal spikes generated by ion collisions. The extended thermal spike duration and localized energy deposition alter defect energetics, increasing migration barriers and formation energies, which suppresses the clustering of point defects into larger, deleterious structures.
item.limitations: The study focuses on simple fcc lattice structures and early-stage defect dynamics; the authors note that the results should not be interpreted as HEAs being intrinsically more radiation resistant in all cases, but rather that complexity is a tunable parameter for modifying transport properties.
item.future_work: The authors propose further exploration to understand how chemistry and composition can alter energy dissipation mechanisms to drive self-recovery from damage states, aiming to design radiation-resistant alloys by controlling coupling strengths and defect energetics at the atomic and electronic levels.
quotes: much slower energy dissipation results in less deleterious defects and consequent slower damage accumulation under ion irradiation.
lower extent of radiation damage produced in NiFe probably relates to the longer thermal spike lifetime due to less efficient heat conduction
